Hachimangu'''|浜松八幡宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

Its origin is said to be '''Kobe Shrine''' (こべじんじゃ), a {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Tōtōmi Province|Q11642130|qid=Q11642130}} of Tōtōmi Province<ref name="official">[http://www.hamamatsuhachimangu.org/ Hamamatsu Hachimangu]</ref>.

== Overview ==
In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}, to pacify {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864|lt=Totoumi}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tamayori-hime-no-Mikoto}}, deity of maritime transport, was enshrined in Kobe-no-sato (around present {{ill|Ozawatari-chō|Q109362601|qid=Q109362601}} in {{ill|Chūō-ku, Hamamatsu|Q117084743|qid=Q117084743|lt=Chūō Ward}}), and in the Heian-period {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} it appears as Kobe Shrine<ref name="about"/>.

In {{ill|938|Q24794|qid=Q24794}} (Tengyō 1), by divine oracle it was moved to the present site. In {{ill|1051|Q19363|qid=Q19363}} (Eishō 6), {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}} (Hachiman Tarō) invited the two Hachiman deities ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Homuda-wake-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okinagatarashi-hime-no-Mikoto}}), and it came to be widely revered by warriors and commoners<ref name="about"/>.

to {{ill|Hamamatsu Castle|Q1152352|qid=Q1152352}} and used this Hachimangu as a ward against the {{ill|Kimon|Q11673539|qid=Q11673539}} direction<ref name="about"/>. During his defeat in the {{ill|Battle of Mikatagahara|Q690464|qid=Q690464}} in {{ill|1572|Q6670|qid=Q6670}} (Genki 3), Ieyasu is said to have fled to this shrine and hidden in the hollow of a camphor tree before the shrine, escaping Takeda troops. Since auspicious clouds ({{ill|Cloud iridescence|Q1328219|qid=Q1328219|lt=zuigun}}) rose from that camphor then, it came to be called "Kumotachi no Kusu" (Cloud-Rising Camphor)<ref name="about"/><ref>[https://www.city.hamamatsu.shizuoka.jp/miryoku/hakken/tanbo/201506-1.html Hamamatsu Hachimangu] - Hamamatsu City</ref><ref>[https://www.at-s.com/facilities/article/view/temple/137771.html Hamamatsu Hachimangu] - Shizuoka Shimbun</ref>. Thereafter Ieyasu designated the shrine as a prayer site for successive Tokugawa generations, dedicating flags, bows, and sacred horses; while he resided in Edo, he sent representatives to worship<ref name="about"/>.
